subject: maths
title: Mensuration
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Mensuration.

concepts.def: The total distance around the outside edge of a two-dimensional shape, found by adding the lengths of all its sides.
The amount of two-dimensional space a shape covers, measured in square units such as square centimetres or square metres.
The distance around the edge of a circle, calculated as pi times the diameter, or 2 times pi times the radius.
The amount of three-dimensional space an object occupies, measured in cubic units such as cubic centimetres.
The total area of all the faces or surfaces of a three-dimensional solid, found by adding the areas of each face.
A region of a circle bounded by two radii and an arc, whose area is a fraction of the whole circle's area based on its angle.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Mensuration — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Mensuration brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Mensuration.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The distance all the way around the edge of a circle is called its:
options: Circumference
Area
Radius
Diameter

mcqs.q: The area of a rectangle is found by:
options: Multiplying length by width
Adding length and width
Multiplying all four sides
Squaring the diagonal

mcqs.q: The volume of a cuboid is calculated as:
options: length x width x height
length x width
2(length + width)
length + width + height

mcqs.q: The area of a circle of radius r is given by:
options: pi x r squared
2 x pi x r
pi x diameter
2 x r

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the area and the perimeter of a shape?
options: Area and perimeter are the same measurement.
Perimeter is the distance around the edge; area is the space inside, measured in square units.
Perimeter is always larger than area.
The area stays the same.

mcqs.q: If the radius of a circle doubles, what happens to its area?
options: The area stays the same.
The area becomes four times as large, because area depends on the radius squared.
Perimeter is always larger than area.
The area simply doubles.

mcqs.q: What units are used to measure volume?
options: Linear units, such as cm.
Square units, such as cm^2.
Cubic units, such as cubic centimetres (cm^3).
The area stays the same.
